questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct grammatically?
questions.question_html: Which of the following statements is correct grammatically?

A.text: A.When he will reach the age of thirty, he will be able to play like his father does.
A.html: When he will reach the age of thirty, he will be able to play like his father does.

B.text: B.When he will reach the age of thirty, he will be able to play as his father does.
B.html: When he will reach the age of thirty, he will be able to play as his father does.

C.text: C.When he reaches the age of thirty, he will be able to play as his father does.
C.html: When he reaches the age of thirty, he will be able to play as his father does.

D.text: D.When he reaches the age of thirty, he will be able to play as his father.
D.html: When he reaches the age of thirty, he will be able to play as his father.

questions.solution_text:
Solution
(c)
Option (c) is the only option which is grammatically correct.
In sentences involving the use of time clause like “when”, future tense cannot be used. In the
given options, option (a) and (b) are ruled out. We can say that “If you drive, I will not accompany
you”. While using ‘as’ and ‘like’, the correct usage is “He plays like his father” or “He plays as his
father does”.
questions.solution_html:

questions.solution_text:
Solution
(c)
The word ‘mercurial’ means ‘quickly changeable’. In the given statement, missing word in the second
